Sentence (English): I purchased this to replace a 15 year-old high end KitchenAid dishwasher that worked pretty flawlessly for a decade and a half.
Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher; odd engineering ] || ---------------- || I purchased this to replace a 15 year-old high end KitchenAid dishwasher that worked pretty flawlessly for a decade and a half. The features and interior engineering of this DWTS424 are good and it seems to clean well. There is a bit of a louder/odd noise when it is in the pro washing mode so I will keep an eye on that – hopefully it was just a pot angled the wrong way. From an engineering standpoint, however, I am disappointed. In these new models, there's a lot more plastic components that were metal in the older models - for example, some of the underbody components, front kickplate, etc. The installation was also vastly more difficult given the way the plastic framing extends down to the floor and through the front of the dishwasher is now present – older models did not have that. It made working with my waterline, drain hose, and electrical hookup very, very difficult. It took an act of Congress for me to figure out how to fish my electrical line from where it comes up through the floor through the underbody components and through the hole in the electrical box underneath. The old model also had a preinstalled hose that gave me flexibility on where the drain line would go – but this model had a very odd location and an angle for the drain line that also made the install very difficult. I ended up having to run the drain line up behind the dishwasher, which did not allow me to push it all the way into the cabinets for a flush install. I'm hopeful that - beyond the engineering and install headaches - this dishwasher will last as long as or longer than as the last, as we've stayed loyal to KitchenAid for all of our major (high end) kitchen appliances.

Sentence (English): I bought a Bosch dishwasher, model SMS4EMI06E, a month ago.
Comments (English): [ Super easy and elegant freestanding dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I bought a Bosch dishwasher, model SMS4EMI06E, a month ago. I'm very happy with it; everything is as described. I use it every day; it's very easy to use, runs quietly, and dishes clean and dry well. The top, third cutlery drawer is fantastic because you can load a lot, and each fork or knife is arranged individually. After washing, it's perfectly clean, unlike with my previous dishwasher, where cutlery was stuffed into a basket and washed separately. The adjustable shelves allow for washing larger pots or tall jars. Furthermore, the folding spikes are very convenient and practical; each dish can be stored securely. There are programs to choose from and many additional functions. You can also shorten the wash by turning on SpeedPerfect+. Both the hour-long program and the eco mode work great for me. I often set it for the night and nothing gets in the way, and in the morning, my dishes are clean. The remote control also works great. I think it's the best purchase.
Comments (Original): [ Super łatwa i elegancka zmywarka wolnostojąca ] || ---------------- || Zmywarkę BOSCH model SMS4EMI06E kupiłam miesiąc temu. Jestem bardzo zadowolona, wszystko jest zgodnie z opisem. Codziennie używam, jest bardzo prosta w obsłudze, cicho pracuje, a naczynia dobrze domyte i wysuszone. Ta górna ,trzecia szuflada na sztućce rewelacja, bo można dużo włożyć i każdy widelec czy nóż osobno ułożony, po umyciu jest doskonale czysty, a nie jak w poprzedniej zmywarce miałam sztućce wepchane do koszyka i rożnie domyte. Regulacja półek pozwala na mycie większych garnków czy np. wysokich słoików. Poza tym składanie kolców jest bardzo wygodne i praktyczne, każde naczynie da się stabilnie ułożyć. Programy do wyboru i sporo funkcji dodatkowych. Można też skracać mycie włączając SpeedPerfect+ dla mnie super sprawdza się zarówno ten godzinny program jak i eco. Często nastawiam na noc i nic nie przeszkadza, a rano mam czyste naczynia. Sterowanie zdalne też działa super.Uważam, że to najlepszy zakup.

Sentence (English): I don't usually write product reviews unless I am annoyed or frusterated, so feel free to take that into account with this review.
Comments (English): [ Newer But Not Necessarily Better ] || ---------------- || I don't usually write product reviews unless I am annoyed or frusterated, so feel free to take that into account with this review. We recently replaced our similar Bosch dishwasher from around 2015. Overall we were mostly pretty happy with the original model, but 10 years seems to be about the life limit and it was time to replace. My initial thoughts were that the two were very similar with only a few changes, however those changes have a big impact on useability. First, for small things, the silverware rack is largely unchanged and still fine, however a bit harder to pull out now. It seems like a sticky mechanism was intentionally added to hold it shut, but it makes pulling out the drawer a bit clunky. Next, also somewhat minor is a redesign the the middle rack to remove one of the rails that holds dishes in place. I'm mixed on that change so far, but it does limit the amount of dishes you can put in the middle rack. The lower rack is mostly unchanged other than a smaller utility tray and a bit better design on the quadrant used for small plates. All of these are minor, and I may learn to appreciate them more as I use the dishwasher, but my major complaint is the overhaul on the dishwasher controls. The older push button controls have been removed in favor of touch control buttons which don't work for beans with a wet dishwaser or wet hands. You'll need to dry your hands and the control panel thoroughly every time you want push a button. Also, the functionality has been really reduced. You can't tell how long the cycle will be anymore, the clock that indicates how much longer the cycle will run is removed, and a lot of basic functionality is now gone. Looking into it more, you now must use the phone app if you want to get any of this functionality back. If you want to have your appliance connect to a phone app, fine. Stupid, but fine. But making someone go track down their phone every time they want to start their dishwasher or check the dishwasher status is an absolute crap user experience. If you want an app, have the ability to control things both from the appliance and from the app. Unless the app will also load the dishwasher then I don't want to go to an app every time I want to set the dishwasher settings. My overall review would probably be 4 stars for the main dishwasher itself, but the change in the controls makes this dishwasher amazingly frusterating to actually use.

Overall we were mostly pretty happy with the original model, but 10 years seems to be about the life limit and it was time to replace.  My initial thoughts were that the two were very similar with only a few changes, however those changes have a big impact on useability.  First, for small things, the silverware rack is largely unchanged and still fine, however a bit harder to pull out now. The lower rack is mostly unchanged other than a smaller utility tray and a bit better design on the quadrant used for small plates.  All of these are minor, and I may learn to appreciate them more as I use the dishwasher, but my major complaint is the overhaul on the dishwasher controls.  The older push button controls have been removed in favor of touch control buttons which don't work for beans with a wet dishwaser or wet hands.  You'll need to dry your hands and the control panel thoroughly every time you want push a button.  Also, the functionality has been really reduced.  You can't tell how long the cycle will be anymore, the clock that indicates how much longer the cycle will run is removed, and a lot of basic functionality is now gone.  Looking into it more, you now must use the phone app if you want to get any of this functionality back.  If you want to have your appliance connect to a phone app, fine.  Stupid, but fine.  But making someone go track down their phone every time they want to start their dishwasher or check the dishwasher status is an absolute crap user experience.  If you want an app, have the ability to control things both from the appliance and from the app.  Unless the app will also load the dishwasher then I don't want to go to an app every time I want to set the dishwasher settings.  My overall review would probably be 4 stars for the main dishwasher itself, but the change in the controls makes this dishwasher amazingly frusterating to actually use.

Sentence (English): We purchased this dishwasher on sale this summer/ fall.
Comments (English): [ Still waiting ] || ---------------- || We purchased this dishwasher on sale this summer/ fall. We had to wait a bit for it to be delivered to the store, but that was fine since we were mid-reno. Installation was difficult for my very handy husband. We ran 2 cycles and then it stopped draining. Because we had to wait to install, we were outside the Lowe's return window and were directed to the ge warranty. Sentence (English): Things I wish I realized before my purchase.
Comments (English): [ Not all 800 models are the same ] || ---------------- || Things I wish I realized before my purchase.The bad1. I thought all 800 models were the same. They aren't. I took dishes to a box store to see if the layout would work for me. It was great and I didn't understand the complaints. This model has different racks that fit less like others mention.2. This model does not allow you to adjust the rinse aid ( ones from other stores might! )3. You can't add an extra rinse either. My dishes constantly smell and taste if not caught like soap and need manual rinses. Only possible solution is to switch to powder and try to figure out the amount and stop using pods.4. The utensil caddy is very bulky and due to the layout already being so limited, if you use it vs. the 3rd rack you fit even less in it.5. They try to make up for the wonky layout with more spigots to hold plates closer, but they sometimes are to close and the larger distance especially on the second rack going the full length would fit dishes better.6. That red spray nozzle on the bottom is a pain to remove and reattach when cleaning out the filter.7. Without a button to release the door, you legit have to pull the handle to open it, I constantly feel I'll rip it out of place, it feels unnecessary and is a bad design.The good1. It is quiet2. If you can figure out the detergent it washes well3. The drying feature does a good job on plastic but I've realized that I don't use much plastic and the 500 model that opens the door to dry would have been more than enough for me.I wouldn't recommend this specific model for the reasons mentioned and wish I figured this out earlier and not 7 ish months as I'm now stuck with it.

Sentence (English): This machine is just okay.
Comments (English): [ Basic, loud and advertised delivery dates untrue ] || ---------------- || This machine is just okay. I bought it solely for Bosche's reputation of reliability. But it's about as basic as you can get. I replaced a 12+ year old contractor grade Whirlpool. The Whirlpool was not great but had more bells and whistles and was much quieter. I only replaced it because it had a heating coil on the bottom and plastic things kept falling out of the cutlery basket onto it and melting. The last time it was very toxic and impossible to clean so I wanted a machine with no heating coils. The Bosche doesn't have exposed heating elements so it made sense. Back to the Bosche: th adjustable shelf mechanism is like the oldest and cheapest version of this. I tested some Lg and Samsung machines and their shelf adjustments are far superior, smooth, east to use, and much more ergonomic. The Bosche's adjustment tooling is just difficult to use. There's NO customization on the shelves, the racks don't collapse or move in anyway. It's difficult to place glasses and small items in the machine because there's no wine glass holders or flat shelves so little items will just fall through the cracks. It is also very very loud because the exterior is quite thin and tinny. I don't recommend this machine unless all you are going for is reliability. It was washes well but like all Bosche reviewers I will tell you nothing is dry when the cycle is complete. Everything is wet. This machine is nothing special. I'll see how it holds up over the next 10 years. Aside from the machine. The advertised delivery dates that Lowe's provides throughout the checkout process are total garbage. We had to wait 3 weeks for the machine that upon starting the checkout process advertised "get it by tomorrow" or some period within two days. So if time is a factor for you. Don't buy from Lowe's. Our delivery experience itself was very pleasant, efficient and professional. She was the best appliance delivery person I have ever experienced (but Lowes uses contractors so it's not like this is anything to do with Lowes and doesn't mean the delivery experience will be consistent)

Sentence (English): There's a lot to like about this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Almost perfect ] || ---------------- || There's a lot to like about this dishwasher. I've owned five dishwasher brands in 25 years as a homeowner, and this one produces the best cleaning results of them all. It is easy to install and use, and the app is generally useful with reminders. The auto setting does what it's supposed to do - who wants to try and figure out the right setting for their dishes? The remote start seems unnecessary, though. One thing I really like is that previous dishwashers would build up a layer of sludge at the bottom under the door. I guess it's difficult to engineer a tight door seal and keep that area clean. This one does not have that problem, making it genuinely more sanitary. The only reason I'm giving this four stars is that the interior space is noticeably smaller than previous dishwashers. Making things even tighter is that third rack. Even reasonable-sized drinking glasses won't fit the top rack when the third rack is in, so we had to remove it. You can drop the top rack down, but if you do that, then plates don't fit in the bottom rack, so that's not a possibility. If Bosch made the top rack drop down just a little bit less in the alternate position, it would help a lot.

We have an open floor plan, and when we run it while watching TV, we never hear it. Also, it gets the dishes clean, even with food that is a bit baked on. It's sleek and looks great. HOWEVER, there are some not great things: (1) It melted our plastic wine glasses, (2) The gaps between the tines in the rack for bowls and glasses are oddly spaced, and items either fall over or would have to be wedged in a too-small space, (3) the rack has holders for 6 stemmed wine glasses, but they're not well-spaced and only 4 wine glasses actually fit while taking up a lot of space, and (4) silverware in the top rack doesn't get very clean unless you leave a lot of space between them and it really only works for knives. Overall we're happy with it, but it's not all it's cracked up to be. One last thing. don't let the "Zeolite drying" thing sway you to purchase this unit. Sentence (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use.
Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Sentence (English): I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together.
Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Sentence (English): They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking.
Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Sentence (English): Drying: This is where opinions differ.
Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Comments (English): A realistic review based on 3 months of actual use. My household situation: A family of 3. We eat at least 2 meals a day at home. I put everything in, including frying pans, soup pots, and even the air fryer basket. 1. Cleaning Power: It is seriously better than human hands. I was skeptical at first, but I ran a cycle with a frying pan used for grilling meat and a pot for kimchi stew together. The grease film, chili powder, and burnt-on residue were all removed. Especially: a pan wiped only with a paper towel after grilling pork belly, and a pot with burnt-on curry and soybean paste stew. They were clean even when put in immediately without soaking. Because the LG Quad Wash sprays water from all sides, it completely strips the bottom of the pot. Honestly, it is cleaner than hand washing. 2. Noise: This surprised me the most. I run it at 11 PM, and it is so quiet that I wonder, "Is it really running?" If the TV is on, you can't hear it at all. You have to put your ear right up in the kitchen to hear the hissing sound of water. Zero stress despite having an open kitchen. 3. The 14-person capacity feels really big. Everything fits in the bottom compartment and finishes in one go: 15 soup bowls, rice bowls, and side dish bowls; 2 frying pans; 1 pot; 6 cups; a basket of cutlery. There is still space left. For a two-person household, it is sufficient to run 2-3 days' worth of laundry all at once. 4. Drying: This is where opinions differ. Since LG uses an automatic door opening + natural drying method, ceramics and stainless steel dry completely. Plastic cups and lids leave a few water droplets. However, since the door opens and steam escapes, they are almost completely dry after 30 minutes to an hour. Those who want a fluffy, heater-drying finish might be disappointed. On the other hand, it uses less electricity and leaves no odor. 5. Smell & Hygiene: This is the real point of satisfaction. Before, even when washing by hand, there was a sponge smell and a water stain smell. Now, there is no smell at all on the cups. The glass cups feel like they come from a hotel. Perhaps because of the high-temperature sterilization, I feel safe even with my child's cups. To be honest about the downsides: 1. Price. Almost 1 million won. It's not cheap. 2. Plastic drying. A few water droplets remain (sometimes need to be wiped). 3. Requires space for the door to open. If there is a shelf above, checking for interference is essential. This product is perfect for: Families stressed about dishwashing every day; those who mainly cook greasy Korean food; those who value quietness; and those who care about kitchen interior design. If you are completely obsessed with hot air drying, consider other brands.

Sentence (English): We used an LG dishwasher before so went with a similar one and it delivered what we were familiar with and looking for.
Comments (English): [ Dishes come out super clean, easy to load and unload the racks, the auto door opening to release hot air ] || ---------------- || We used an LG dishwasher before so went with a similar one and it delivered what we were familiar with and looking for. There were a few improvements too. I like how the front door opens by itself a little in the last 30 minutes of drying. The fans are still working and it pushes the hot air outside. The dishes come out perfectly clean, no water stains, and perfectly dry. You do need to be careful not to leave anything on the counter that can be affected by the hot air to come out (e.g., bread, fruit, food). In our old dishwasher, we used to have issues with our bottom rack when plates or bowls moved, it would block the blade underneath. This one seemed to have solved that problem and the rack doesn't have the wide openings to make that possible. The normal cycle is sufficient with most dishes and the heavy wash setting works well on pots with oil and grease stains. The bottom filter is easily accessible to remove and clean. We also love how it is operating quietly so you can have a conversation in the kitchen while it is running. The connection to phone and app functionality is also useful as I get notifications when the rinse-aid is running low or a washing cycle is complete. Overall, we like how it is easy to load and unload the racks, how clean the dishes come out, and the method of drying with the auto opening door.
